newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel leader confirms talks with government.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel leader confirms talks with government.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in Lima confirmed on Monday they were prepared to restart face-to-face talks with the government on Tuesday.

"The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement manifests it total willingness to start conversations on Tuesday," rebel spokesman Nestor Cerpa Cartolini said in a walkie-talkie conversation from inside the Japanese ambassador's residence where the guerrillas are holding the hostages.

Cerpa said the MRTA had always been willing to hold talks but reiterated it would not relinquish its "unrevocable" position. "The beginning of the talks does not necessarily mean the beginning of the solution to the conflict," he said.
President Alberto Fujimori has flatly rejected the MRTA's principal demand, the release of some 400 jailed comrades.

Cerpa said Fujimori's statement in London "that if the conversations fail it would be a step towards the use of force, constitutes a veiled threat trying to turn it at the same time into a pyschological weapon."

Fujimori announced Sunday that conversations were set to resume on Tuesday between government negotiator Domingo Palermo and Cerpa's deputy Roli Rojas, known by his nom de guerre "El Arabe" (The Arab).
